text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma forces KPN's PTT Telecom to reduce its stake in cable company Casema. (p1)
- Majority of MPs against basing pensions on the average wage earned throughout an employee's lifetime. (p1)
- 300 employees at Smit Lloyd oppose 18 pct voluntary pay cut to improve the company's competitiveness. (p3)
- ABN Amro bank aims for considerable growth in South America. (p3)
- Sylvia Toth, chairman and majority shareholder in temp agency Content, reduces stake from 50.3 pct to 19.28 pct. (p3)
- Container transport by inland waterway will grow 15 pct this year. (p3)
- Biochemicals and food group Gist-Brocades buys Brazil's Colombo Industria e Comercio. (p4)
- Dutch producer prices rise 0.9 pct in September compared to August, mainly due to high petrol prices. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Unions find employers paying higher wages voluntarily. (p1)
- Cargill in Amsterdam has been supplied with genetically manipulated soybeans for ten days. (p1)
- Parliament is doubtful on sending troops to Zaire. (p1)
- Journalist Haye Thomas (60) -- correspondent for NOS television in Brussels -- dies of heart attack. (p1)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Natural gas company Gasunie on the verge of finalising 200 million guilder contract with Czech Republic. (p1)
- Alarming rise in cases of repetitive strain injury (RSI). (p3)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM mulls taking a 25 pct interest in Indonesian carrier Garuda. (p23)
- International telecom provider Versatel Telecom files a complaint with EU against PTT Telecom's misuse of its monopoly position. (p23)
TROUW
- Producers and importers of alcoholic beverages demand an immediate stop to alcohol moderation ad campaign. (p1)
- Spain's national airlines Iberia says it is in advanced negotiations with KLM on forming European airlines group. (p13)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Chances of a railway strike grow as workers in Rotterdam area vote against new pay and conditions proposal. (p5)
- Hungarian commentators say ABN AMRO bank has paid a high price for the Magyar Hitel Bank. (p11)
- Philips Electronics studying closure of its main plant in Brazil and transfering to a country with lower wage costs. (p13)
